findings.title: Interpolating before the $__range guard splits queries that must stay whole
findings.body: runSplitQuery now runs datasource.applyTemplateVariables before querySupportsSplitting. That helper refuses to split expressions that still contain [$__range], [$__range_s], or [$__range_ms], because those macros must be resolved against the original request range (the comment says backend interpolation on a split range is wrong). templateSrv.replace, which applyTemplateVariables uses, substitutes $__range* from the parent request before that check, so isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer matches and the query is day-split. Each chunk is then executed with the full-dashboard duration already baked in (for example [7d] on a 1-day window), which over-counts range aggregations and multiplies Loki load. The same substitution also happens in runShardSplitQuery before it delegates to runSplitQuery, so the shard path has the same hole.

findings.title: Pre-interpolating range vars breaks stream-shard selector rewrite
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now expands variables with applyTemplateVariables before interpolateShardingSelector rewrites the stream selector (line 154). interpolateShardingSelector inserts the shard matcher and `| drop __stream_shard__` by replacing the `{...}` selector only. If a range like [$__auto] is still attached to that selector, the rewrite keeps a valid range vector; after this change [$__auto] is already `5m`, so the range is left behind the inserted pipeline. The new test locks in the result: `count_over_time({a="b", __stream_shard__=~"20|10"} | drop __stream_shard__[5m])`, which is invalid LogQL (count_over_time requires a range vector, and [5m] is bound to the drop stage). Sharded metric queries whose range or step is a variable will fail or return errors.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables runs again on already interpolated shard requests
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery already maps every target through applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters) and then calls runSplitQuery on each shard subrequest. runSplitQuery applies the same function again, still passing request.filters. applyTemplateVariables is not idempotent when filters are present: ad-hoc matchers are appended to expr on every call, so each sharded subquery gets duplicate label matchers and can be rejected by Loki. The updated shard test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called 5 times (once up front plus once per group inside runSplitQuery), which confirms the re-entry, but nothing asserts that filters or escaped matchers survive a second pass.
